Why Cheaper Restaurant Food May Stay Off The Menu This Year

Dining out is likely to remain expensive as uneven relief in ingredient costs keeps restaurant margins under pressure.

Lower cattle prices have provided some relief this past summer, but soaring cooking-oil and grain costs, along with a rebound in chicken prices, leave little room for broad menu price cuts, according to a note from BofA restaurant analyst Sara Senatore on Friday.

Cattle prices fell 9% from a year earlier in the third quarter, reversing a 9.8% increase in the second quarter, Senatore wrote. But the futures market points to a 1.4% rise from a year earlier in the fourth quarter and a 3.9% rise from the preceding three months.

The decline in cattle prices comes as major restaurant operators face elevated prices for a wide variety of inputs. Soybean oil prices rose 35.7% in the third quarter, while wheat gained 19.6% and corn increased 10%.

Chicken prices are also turning higher after a sharp decline over the last year. Breast prices were up 4% from October a year earlier, compared with a 36% decline in July. Wing prices rose 2%, reversing a 28% drop over the same period.

French right-wing politician Éric Zemmour said Sunday that violent protests and looting the previous day revealed "the true face of the Great Replacement," citing Palestinian, Algerian and Moroccan flags among demonstrators and alleging ties to antifascist groups and left-wing lawmakers.

During an appearance on French news network LCI, Zemmour said: "What we saw yesterday is the true face of the Great Replacement. It has an appearance: hordes of North African and African barbarians who rampage through cities."

🇫🇷🔴 The Great Replacement is driving the French riots, says right-wing politician Éric Zemmour. "I believe that what we saw yesterday is the true face of the Great Replacement. It has an appearance: hordes of North African and African barbarians who ransack cities." Follow: @RMXnews

Zemmour, a former journalist and author who leads the Reconquête party, has long promoted the "Great Replacement," which he uses to describe native European populations being demographically supplanted by non-European immigrants, particularly from Muslim-majority countries, Africa, and Asia. The topic is openly discussed in France, including among intellectuals, academics, politicians, and even Michel Houellebecq, arguably the country's most celebrated living author.

Zemmour's remarks referred to massive riots on Oct. 17 that occurred in French cities across the country, where protests over the cost of living and public services turned into some of the country's most violent demonstrations in years. Videos of burning buildings, looted stores, and violent clashes with police were spread across social media.

Zemmour's remarks came at a time when U.S. officials, including Donald Trump, have remarked on the riots as well.

"France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country. Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!" wrote Trump.

Vice President JD Vance also wrote on X: "Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn't listen."

Zemmour, who finished fourth in the 2022 presidential election, has remained a prominent voice on immigration ahead of France's next national vote, but his right-wing rival, Le Pen, is heavily favored to win the presidency. Zemmour typically polls around 5 percent in the first round.

title: Toyota's "Next Gen" Corolla Built In China Will Offer Multiple Powertrains
desc:
Toyota's "Next Gen" Corolla Built In China Will Offer Multiple Powertrains

Toyota is taking a more flexible approach to electrification, preparing to launch a redesigned Corolla in China in 2028 that can be manufactured with gasoline, hybrid or fully electric powertrains, according to Nikkei Asia. The move comes as automakers increasingly rethink their EV strategies amid slowing growth, fierce competition and uncertainty about how quickly consumers will abandon combustion engines.

Nikkei writes that the new Corolla will be built through Toyota's FAW joint venture using a multipathway platform designed to streamline manufacturing and reduce costs. Rather than committing to a single propulsion technology, Toyota will be able to adjust production based on consumer demand and market conditions.

The shift comes as Toyota struggles in China, where August sales fell 23% year over year to 118,449 vehicles, including Lexus. Domestic competition has intensified, pricing pressure has increased and profitability has suffered. Toyota is also developing longer-range Lexus EVs and extended-range electric vehicles that use gasoline engines to generate electricity.

More broadly, the global EV industry has experienced a significant reality check over the last several years. After an initial wave of enthusiasm fueled by government subsidies, ambitious emissions targets and aggressive manufacturer forecasts, EV adoption has become increasingly uneven. Sales continue to grow globally, particularly in China, but demand in several Western markets has fallen short of earlier expectations, prompting automakers to delay investments, scale back production targets and reconsider plans to eliminate combustion engines entirely.

Companies that once promised an almost exclusively electric future are increasingly embracing hybrids and other transitional technologies. High vehicle prices, charging infrastructure limitations, changing government incentives and consumer concerns about range have complicated the transition. Toyota's latest strategy reflects a growing recognition across the industry that the future of transportation may involve a broader mix of technologies than many manufacturers anticipated just a few years ago.

title: German Power Supply Startups Exit Market As Wholesale Prices Soar
desc:
German Power Supply Startups Exit Market As Wholesale Prices Soar

Authored by Michael Kern via OilPrice,

Two startup electricity retailers in Germany have recently announced they would cease operations as spiking wholesale prices amid the gas price surge are pressuring the industry again, and this time the pressure is compounded by plans for renewable policy changes.

Renewable electricity provider Grüüün, part of Münch Energie Group, early this month said it would discontinue servicing about 200,000 residential customers as of October 31, 2026, and these will now have to switch to other providers.

Grüüün, which launched operations in 2024, attributed its decision to fold to Germany's proposed changes to its renewable energy policy, including the upcoming overhaul of the Renewable Energy Sources Act (EEG 2027), the government's focus on gas-fired power generation, and rising grid charges that have disrupted its long-term pricing structure.

Another startup, Berlin-based Stromee, has also reportedly exited the German retail market after a local utility in western Germany, SWK Energie GmbH, said this week that it had taken over power and gas customers "in the low five-digit range."

The wholesale power price spikes and the regulatory shifts in Germany have made the sector vulnerable, with market exits reminiscent of the 2022 energy crisis when numerous small providers were forced to fold, Bloomberg notes.

This year, Germany is also facing the start of the winter with historically low levels of gas in storage sites. As of October 15, Germany's gas storage sites were 60% full, well below the EU average of 74%, according to data by Gas Infrastructure Europe. The EU storage levels are at their lowest since at least 2011, raising concerns that a cold winter could lead to gas shortages.

Thanks to diversified import capabilities, Germany doesn't face a gas supply shortage despite record-low levels of natural gas in storage sites, one of the biggest German gas importers, VNG, said at the end of last month.

Low stockpiles in Germany's vast storage, the world's fourth-largest, have prompted concerns about supply security if the coming winter turns out much colder than previous winters.

title: Shocker: Teens Put Down Their Phones For Summer Camp, Mental Health Improves
desc:
Shocker: Teens Put Down Their Phones For Summer Camp, Mental Health Improves

For two to three-and-a-half weeks, teenagers at a Maine summer camp traded their devices for outdoor activities and face-to-face friendships. By the end, their mental health had improved - with the largest gains among those who arrived struggling.

The findings add to research suggesting that relief from constant connectivity can produce benefits surprisingly quickly. They also raise a question - How much of it depends on what replaces the screen?

The study, published in Mental Health & Prevention, assessed 192 adolescents attending a device-free residential camp. Researchers included scientists from Sapien Labs and UC San Diego.

Participants' composite mental-health scores improved by an average of 10.1 points between arrival and departure. Those starting with mental-health struggles recorded a median improvement of 27 points. These are changes on the study's questionnaire scale, not percentage improvements or evidence that a psychiatric condition was cured.

The strongest gains involved adaptability and resilience. Campers also reported better focus and less worry and restlessness. Forty-four percent said they felt a stronger sense of belonging at camp than at school; 40% found making friends easier.

A session cost $4,900 to $7,900. Fewer than one in 10 campers arrived in the study's distressed or struggling range, against more than half of US teens on the same measure, and nearly a quarter saw their scores fall by more than five points. Sapien notes that there was no control group - so we can't know for sure whether removing devices caused the improvement, vs. how much came from exercise, sleep, friendship and the broader camp experience.

That said, there's been similar research...

A 2024 Danish study in JAMA Network Open randomly assigned 89 families, including 181 children and adolescents, either to reduce recreational screen use or continue their usual habits. For two weeks, the intervention families handed over smartphones and tablets and were instructed to limit leisure screen use to three hours per week per person. Basic phones preserved calls and texting.

Children in those families showed greater improvement in behavioral difficulties, particularly emotional symptoms and peer problems, alongside better prosocial behavior. The overall effect was moderate by conventional statistical standards.

This provides stronger evidence that changing screen habits can help. Still, the children averaged roughly nine years old, parents knew which group they were in and supplied the behavioral ratings, and the experiment did not establish whether the benefits were lasting.

In a 2014 study led by UCLA researchers, 51 sixth-graders spent five days at an outdoor camp without screens. Compared with 54 schoolmates who continued their normal routines, campers improved more at recognizing emotions from facial expressions and other nonverbal cues. That measured a social skill, rather than depression or anxiety. The groups were not randomly assigned, and outdoor activities and greater personal interaction accompanied the screen break. Nevertheless, the finding suggests that even a brief change in daily habits can affect how children read other people.

A 2025 randomized trial in PNAS Nexus enrolled 467 people in an experiment blocking internet access on their smartphones for two weeks. Calls, texts and internet access through other devices remained available. Researchers found improvements in mental health, wellbeing and objectively tested sustained attention. Participants reported spending more time socializing in person, exercising and being outdoors. Just 119 participants met the prespecified compliance threshold of keeping the block active for at least 10 days. The average participant was 32, so these results cannot simply be transferred to teenagers.

There is also emerging evidence from the Maine camp itself. A September 2026 preprint examined brain-wave recordings from 30 campers and reported changes associated with some improvements in wellbeing. However, it was a small, uncontrolled pilot, had not been peer-reviewed, and came from the same broader camp project. Meanwhile, a 2025 SMART Schools study compared 1,227 adolescents across 30 English schools. Students at schools with restrictive phone policies used phones less during school, but did not report better mental wellbeing. Their overall weekday and weekend phone use was not significantly different.

Maine campers who said they exercised more at camp gained 17.4 points on average, against 4.8 for those who exercised less. Those who felt a stronger sense of belonging gained 15 points, against 5.8 for those whose sense of belonging fell. None of those gaps reached statistical significance, and the scores were taken on the last day of camp, so whether the gains lasted after campers went home is unknown.

title: European Parliament Condemns Muslim Brotherhood, Calls For Crackdown on Islamist Influence
desc:
European Parliament Condemns Muslim Brotherhood, Calls For Crackdown on Islamist Influence

Authored by AG News Staff via American Greatness,

The European Parliament has approved a resolution condemning the Muslim Brotherhood and calling for stronger action against Islamist influence in European institutions. The resolution is a significant development in the continent's efforts to combat political extremism.

The center-right European People's Party spearheaded the resolution, which follows the Trump administration's designation of the Muslim Brotherhood and four affiliated branches as terrorist organizations.

French European Parliament member Céline Imart, who sponsored the measure, celebrated the vote as a breakthrough.

"This is a historic victory because it is a European first," Imart said, describing the resolution as Europe's first parliamentary action specifically confronting Islamist infiltration and the Muslim Brotherhood.

The resolution warns that organized Islamist networks threaten democratic institutions, religious freedoms, the rule of law and equality between men and women.

It calls for greater scrutiny of foreign funding, particularly involving organizations connected to Qatar and Turkey, and increased transparency surrounding European Union funding of groups suspected of Muslim Brotherhood ties.

Lawmakers also urged the European Council to consider whether Brotherhood-linked individuals and organizations should be added to the EU's terrorist list.

Lorenzo Vidino, director of George Washington University's Program on Extremism, said conservative lawmakers overwhelmingly supported the measure, while significant portions of the political left opposed it.

Imart criticized socialist and far-left lawmakers for boycotting negotiations on the resolution.

Security experts described the vote as an important first step toward confronting Islamist organizations accused of exploiting European democratic institutions.

"This resolution is where the pushback begins against Islamist entryism in Europe," said Edmund Fitton-Brown, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies.

However, the European Network Against Racism condemned the resolution, calling it discriminatory and warning that it could unfairly target Muslim communities and civil society organizations.

The Parliament emphasized that protecting Muslims from discrimination remains essential while distinguishing religious freedom from organized Islamist political activity.

Unlike the Trump administration's terrorist designations, the European resolution is not binding legislation. Additional action by EU institutions would be required to implement its recommendations.

Imart vowed to continue pressing European leaders to act.

"This vote is a victory, but it is also a starting point," she said.

title: Veterans Blast 'Palestine Poppy' As Hijacking Of Remembrance Symbol, A Week After Protesters Trampled Battle Of Britain Wreaths
desc:
Veterans Blast 'Palestine Poppy' As Hijacking Of Remembrance Symbol, A Week After Protesters Trampled Battle Of Britain Wreaths

Pro-Palestinian campaigners are selling a "Palestine Poppy" in the green, red, white and black of the Palestinian flag ahead of Remembrance Sunday, and British veterans say it hijacks the country's day of mourning for its war dead, GB News reports.

The badge is on eBay for £1.74 each, and the Mail counts more than 1,200 sold so far. The group behind it calls the poppies "a symbol of solidarity and remembrance for the ongoing struggle of the Palestinian people and their fight for justice." Sales are not-for-profit, with a "small donation" going to charities in Palestine and to groups seeking to end "the occupation and war crimes through legal routes."

Retired Army officer and defense analyst Lt. Col. Stuart Crawford told GB News the badge is an attempt to "ride on the coat-tails of the familiar red poppy."

"The Remembrance poppy is avowedly apolitical," he said, while the Palestine version is "unashamedly political, designed to divide rather than unite."

Former Royal Navy officer Stuart Fawcett tied it to last weekend's march in London.

"Now, we see them hijacking our national symbol of remembrance," he told the broadcaster.

The march he means took place Saturday, Oct. 10. The Met Police said it made 20 arrests, six of them for criminal damage after protesters climbed the Battle of Britain memorial on the Embankment, where wreaths at the base were trampled and destroyed. Others were held for showing placards backing Palestine Action, a proscribed group, and for a racially aggravated public order offense after a woman was seen making a Nazi salute, Jewish News reports, citing the force.

Conservative MP Nick Timothy called the protesters "scum," and Lord Hannan asked what they had against the Battle of Britain pilots. Deputy Assistant Commissioner Carl Galvin, who ran the operation, said the march's timing near the third anniversary of the Oct. 7 attack raised the risk to community relations.

The poppy's website carries the slogan "From the river to the sea, Palestine will be free," which critics read as a denial of Israel's right to exist, the Mail notes. It also calls those killed or displaced in Gaza victims of "genocide," a label Israel and its supporters reject.

title: Is Turkiye Plotting A Coup In Brotherly Azerbaijan?
desc:
Is Turkiye Plotting A Coup In Brotherly Azerbaijan?

Authored by Andrew Korybko via Substack,

A now-deleted Azeri article over the weekend, whose initial publication was perceived by many Turks as having been state-approved, prompted a complaint from the Turkish Embassy in Baku and worsened mutual suspicions among these fraternal people of what the other's government is up to.

The Turkish Embassy in Baku released a statement over the weekend denying a local media report that former spy chief-turned-Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan's picture with members of the "Youth Assistance Foundation" during his latest trip to Baku to attend a multilateral event was proof of a secret meeting. The report has since been deleted, but the gist was that the aforesaid group and others are operating under Turkiye's influence to weaponize the recent pro-hijab protests for regime change purposes.

For background, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's condemnation of unnamed states' hijab bans in his UNGA speech last month preceded the entry into force of Azerbaijan's new school uniform policy that was interpreted by some administrators in that way, thus prompting a wave of protests. His Azerbaijani counterpart Ilham Aliyev then accused unnamed states of meddling in Azeri affairs during a speech to members of the ruling party. Some Azeris suspect that Turkish activists organized the protests.

Ahead of the previously mentioned event in Baku, Aliyev dispatched his national airline to pick up his Israeli counterpart on a plane named after the Azeri-Turkish alliance to fly him to to Baku across Turkish airspace despite Ankara banning all Israeli flights, which some Turks considered to be a snub. Since then, critical articles about Turkiye have appeared in Azeri media, which is considered by some to be state-influenced. This further fueled their ongoing social media disputes. Here are three background briefings:

* 5 October: "The Azeri-Turkish Brotherhood Is Going Through Some Trouble"

* 14 October: "The Azeri-Turkish Brotherhood Is Being Tested By Azerbaijan's Pro-Hijab Protests"

* 17 October: "Aliyev Used Israeli President Herzog To Take Three Jabs At Erdogan"

Two driving forces are behind this unprecedented dispute between these fraternal nations that consider themselves to be "one nation, two states". These are Turkiye's discomfort with Azerbaijan's de facto alliance with Israel, with which Turkiye has been in a rivalry since October 7th, and Azerbaijan's discomfort what some perceive to be Turkiye's Neo-Ottoman plans. Some Turks now suspect that Israel is behind Azerbaijan's alleged hijab ban while some Azeris suspect that Turkiye is behind the protests.

Moreover, some Azeris worry that Turkiye's suspected plans to turn August 2025's "Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity" into a Turkish-led NATO logistics corridor along Russia's southern periphery could spark a Ukrainian-like war, while some Turks believe that Israel planted these fears. The hijab issue was therefore only the spark for getting Azeris and Turks to air out their grievances against one another on social media, not the root cause, but it now seems to have taken on a life of its own.

This background contextualizes the earlier cited article that was deleted after the Turkish Embassy's complaint. While its veracity is unclear, what's much more certain is that its publication was probably greenlit to signal to Turkiye to rein in its social media activists who've directly involved themselves in Azerbaijan's hijab debate, which Baku tacitly considers to be meddling given the protests that have since followed. If they don't soon stop, then Azeris might consider this to be a betrayal of their brotherhood.
